reasoning_traces.think:
Additive ambiguity is the preferred choice for compositional risk management because it avoids violating individual class-conditional error caps, unlike product ambiguity which can exceed them. This property makes it suitable for hierarchical gate structures in GSI (per-market-type) and GSE (sequential filtering). Market-conditional beta further refines the trade-off by adapting the nonconformity threshold to each market's specific characteristics, recovering more picks while maintaining overall accuracy. The multi-gate additive control framework provides a scalable way to combine independent decisions, ensuring that no single gate dominates the portfolio.
